Agentic - 1.pdf.title: Not Every AI That Uses Tools Is an Agent

Agentic - 2.pdf.title: Chatbot vs Workflow vs Agent

Agentic - 3.pdf.summary: A visual introduction to the components that make an agent useful.

Agentic - 4.pdf.summary: Follow an agent through decisions, actions and observations as it works toward a goal.

Agentic - 5.pdf.summary: Consider when an agent helps and when a simpler approach fits the task.

Agentic - 6.pdf.title: How AI Agents Use Tools

Agentic - 8.pdf.summary: Understand working and long-term memory, then follow how agents store, retrieve, correct and delete information.

Agentic - 13.pdf.summary: Explains how agents plan research, explore and compare sources, verify evidence, and synthesize a cited report.

Agentic - 18.pdf.summary: Explains how A2UI lets agents describe interactive interfaces that host applications render using their own components.

Agentic - 19.pdf.title: How Does a Frontend Keep Up with an Agent While It Works?
Agentic - 19.pdf.summary: Introduces AG-UI as the live communication layer for streaming agent events, synchronizing state, and exchanging tools and user input.

Agentic - 20.pdf.title: Why Can the Same Model Feel Like a Completely Different Agent?
Agentic - 20.pdf.summary: Explains how an agent harness combines tools, state, runtime controls and tracing to turn a model into an operating agent.

Agentic - 21.pdf.title: Your Agent Worked Once. Does That Mean It Works?
Agentic - 21.pdf.summary: Introduces agent evaluations that use task contracts, repeated trials, traces and graders to measure outcomes, safety and cost.

Agentic - 22.pdf.title: Why Does an Agent Forget Everything Next Time?
Agentic - 22.pdf.summary: Explains how short-term and long-term memory retain selected information and retrieve it into context for future work.

Agentic - 23.pdf.title: Should an Agent Plan Before It Acts?
Agentic - 23.pdf.summary: Shows when agents should plan, how to break goals into ordered actions, and when new evidence calls for replanning.

Agentic - 24.pdf.title: What Happens Between the Goal and the Action?
Agentic - 24.pdf.summary: Introduces ReAct, reflection and search as control loops for choosing actions, checking results and improving decisions.

Agentic - 25.pdf.title: Why Does Agent Security Matter?
Agentic - 25.pdf.summary: Examines prompt injection and tool-related risks, with trust boundaries, limited permissions, approvals and tracing to control agent actions.

GenAI - 1.pdf.title: What exactly IS Artificial Intelligence?

GenAI - 11.pdf.summary: Explore how generative AI supports everyday work, creative tasks and hobbies.

GenAI - 12.pdf.summary: Introduce AI agents through a simple example of an assistant that acts on a request.

GenAI - 15.pdf.summary: Explain how vector embeddings represent words and their meaning as numbers.

GenAI - 16.pdf.summary: Compare fine-tuning and retrieval-augmented generation as approaches to customizing an AI system.

GenAI - 17.pdf.title: Multimodal AI: AI That Sees, Hears & Understands!
GenAI - 17.pdf.summary: Introduce AI systems that work across text, images and audio.

GenAI - 18.pdf.title: Generative AI for Code: From Idea to App!
GenAI - 18.pdf.summary: Explore how generative AI can assist with writing, debugging and explaining code.

System Design - 1.pdf.title: What Is AI System Design?
System Design - 1.pdf.summary: Learn how data, models, tools, and application logic work together to turn an AI model into a useful, reliable product.

System Design - 2.pdf.title: Before You Draw Boxes, Define Success
System Design - 2.pdf.summary: Define the user’s job, system constraints, and measurable success criteria before writing a practical design brief for an AI policy assistant.

System Design - 3.pdf.title: Choose the Right System Shape
System Design - 3.pdf.summary: Compare rules, predictive models, retrieval workflows, and agents to choose an architecture that fits the required output and execution path.

System Design - 4.pdf.title: Two Paths. One Working System.
System Design - 4.pdf.summary: Trace how data preparation and serving connect in a policy assistant and demand forecast, including artifacts, tool responsibilities, and quality measures.

System Design - 5.pdf.title: Who Can Ask for What?
System Design - 5.pdf.summary: Design API contracts that validate requests, establish identity, and enforce permissions before protected data reaches the model.

System Design - 6.pdf.title: What Counts as a Successful Result?
System Design - 6.pdf.summary: Turn AI requirements into realistic test cases, scoring rules, and explicit release criteria.

System Design - 7.pdf.title: What Exactly Are We Predicting?
System Design - 7.pdf.summary: Define the customer population, prediction moment, observation window, and outcome that make a precise training example.

System Design - 8.pdf.title: Is the Data Fit for This Job?

System Design - 9.pdf.title: Can Your Model See the Future?
System Design - 9.pdf.summary: Design training and evaluation splits that respect time, entity boundaries, and the information available when predictions are made.

System Design - 10.pdf.title: Same Feature Name. Same Meaning?
System Design - 10.pdf.summary: Define and version reproducible features so training and serving use consistent meanings, time windows, and available data.

System Design - 11.pdf.title: A Score Still Needs a Decision
System Design - 11.pdf.summary: Compare a learned model with a baseline and choose thresholds using precision, recall, error costs, and review capacity.

System Design - 12.pdf.title: Can You Reconstruct Yesterday's Model?
System Design - 12.pdf.summary: Connect retained data, experiment runs, fitted artifacts, and decision policies in an inspectable release manifest.

System Design - 13.pdf.title: Score a Whole Cohort Without Exposing Half a Result
System Design - 13.pdf.summary: Design batch inference with pinned inputs, stable partitions, safe retries, complete validation, and atomic publication.

System Design - 14.pdf.title: The User Is Waiting for the Prediction
System Design - 14.pdf.summary: Design an online prediction service with valid features, bounded latency, capacity limits, and fallback behavior.

System Design - 15.pdf.title: Do You Actually Need a Feature Store?
System Design - 15.pdf.summary: Choose feature infrastructure from reuse, historical retrieval, freshness, and operational ownership requirements.

System Design - 16.pdf.title: A Changing Input Is a Clue
System Design - 16.pdf.summary: Distinguish data drift from model quality changes and design alerts around delayed outcomes and label coverage.

System Design - 17.pdf.title: Find Candidates. Then Order Them.
System Design - 17.pdf.summary: Design recommendation retrieval and ranking, then evaluate relevance, availability, coverage, and latency at each stage.

System Design - 18.pdf.title: Connect the Whole ML Service
System Design - 18.pdf.summary: Connect data, features, training, release, serving, and monitoring through explicit contracts and recovery paths.

System Design - 19.pdf.title: A Prompt Is an Interface
System Design - 19.pdf.summary: Build and version a prompt contract with distinct instructions, request data, evidence, output rules, and evaluation cases.

System Design - 20.pdf.title: Valid JSON Is Only the Start
System Design - 20.pdf.summary: Route structured model outputs through completion, refusal, schema, meaning, and authorization checks.

System Design - 21.pdf.title: Which Model Fits This Job?

System Design - 22.pdf.title: Fix the Cause of the Error

System Design - 24.pdf.title: The First Word Is Not Done

System Design - 25.pdf.title: An Answer Starts at the Source

System Design - 26.pdf.title: Design Chunks and Metadata
System Design - 26.pdf.summary: Choose chunk boundaries and metadata that preserve meaning, source references, permissions, and document versions.

System Design - 27.pdf.title: Build and Update the Index
System Design - 27.pdf.summary: Design a vector index with consistent embeddings, controlled version activation, reliable updates, and explicit deletion behavior.

System Design - 28.pdf.title: Retrieve and Rerank Evidence
System Design - 28.pdf.summary: Combine lexical and vector retrieval, rerank eligible evidence, and assemble context within separate candidate and token budgets.

System Design - 29.pdf.title: Enforce Access and Support Claims
System Design - 29.pdf.summary: Authorize evidence before generation, connect claims to supporting passages, and handle denied, missing, or conflicting sources.

System Design - 30.pdf.title: Evaluate the Complete RAG Path
System Design - 30.pdf.summary: Diagnose failures across the RAG pipeline and compare controlled changes using retrieval, answer quality, access, latency, and cost measures.
